**The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle: A Species on the Brink**

The Asian giant softshell turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor’s giant softshell turtle, is one of the largest freshwater turtles in the world. Reaching lengths of up to 2 meters (6.5 feet) and weighing as much as 100 kilograms (220 pounds), this elusive species inhabits slow-moving rivers, estuaries, and wetlands across parts of Southeast and South Asia, including India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, and Vietnam (IUCN Red List). Distinctive for its leathery, rubber-like shell and flat, wide head with upward-facing eyes, the turtle spends most of its life buried in riverbeds—emerging only briefly to breathe and feed.

Critically endangered since 2007, the Asian giant softshell turtle faces severe threats from habitat destruction, dam construction, pollution, and accidental capture in fishing nets (WWF). Its naturally low reproductive rate—females likely lay only one clutch per year—makes recovery particularly difficult. Additionally, wetland drainage for agriculture and urban development has destroyed much of its natural habitat, while illegal wildlife trade further threatens its survival.

Conservation efforts are underway, though limited. In 2020, a significant discovery was made in Vietnam’s Dong Nai Biosphere Reserve, where researchers captured and tagged a live specimen—rare confirmation the species still survives in the wild (Asian Turtle Conservation Network). Breeding programs in captivity, such as in India and Cambodia, aim to boost population numbers, but long-term success remains uncertain.

![Asian giant softshell turtle basking](https://www.savethecritters.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Cantors-Turtle.jpg)  
*Image source: Save the Critters – A rare sighting of Pelochelys cantorii.*

![Habitat of Asian giant softshell turtle](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Tobias-Thomson/publication/338729321/figure/fig1/AS:869658329972736@1584184891733/Typical-habitat-of-Pelochelys-cantorii-in-river-systems-of-South-East-Asia.jpg)  
*Image: Typical river habitat of the species in Southeast Asia (ResearchGate).*

Despite its massive size, the Asian giant softshell turtle remains largely hidden and poorly understood. Its future depends heavily on intensified conservation measures, including habitat protection, anti-poaching enforcement, and public awareness campaigns.

---

**Bibliography**

IUCN Red List. “*Pelochelys cantorii*.” *The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, 2022, https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/18963/109889689.

Turtle Conservation Fund. “Cantor's Giant Softshell Turtle.” *World Wildlife Fund*, https://www.worldwildlife.org/species/cantors-giant-softshell-turtle.

Asian Turtle Conservation Network. “Rare Live Specimen of *Pelochelys cantorii* Found in Vietnam.” *ATCN*, 2020, https://www.asianturtlenetwork.org/research/rare-discovery-in-vietnam.
